system_overview: This specification models a simple concurrent algorithm from Lamport's 'Teaching Concurrency' article (ACM SIGACT News, Volume 40, Issue 1, March 2009). The algorithm demonstrates a fundamental property of concurrent systems: N processes are arranged in a logical circle, each process writes a value to its own shared register and then reads its left neighbor's register, and the specification proves that after all processes terminate, at least one process must have observed the value written by its neighbor.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes, numbered 0 through N-1, arranged logically in a circle. Each process has a shared register that it writes to and that its right neighbor reads. Process i's left neighbor is the process at position (i-1) modulo N, and its right neighbor is at position (i+1) modulo N.
state_variables: The system tracks two arrays, each indexed by process number (0 through N-1): (1) a shared write-register array where each process stores a value of either 0 or 1, and (2) a local read-result array where each process stores the value it read from its left neighbor's register (also 0 or 1). Additionally, a program counter array tracks which step each process is currently at.
initial_state: Both arrays are initialized to all zeros. Every process begins at its first step (the write step).
actions: Each process executes two steps in sequence: (1) Write step: the process sets its own entry in the shared register array to 1. (2) Read step: the process reads the value in its left neighbor's shared register (the neighbor at position (i-1) modulo N) and stores the result in its own local read-result entry, then terminates. After all processes have terminated, a stuttering step allows the system to remain in its final state indefinitely (to prevent the model checker from reporting deadlock).
safety_properties: The key correctness property is: whenever all processes have terminated, at least one process must have read the value 1 from its left neighbor. Informally, since all processes write 1 to their registers and then read their left neighbor, it is impossible for all reads to return 0 -- at least one process must see the write from its neighbor. The specification also includes a type-correctness invariant ensuring the arrays and program counters remain within their expected ranges, and an inductive invariant that strengthens the correctness property to be provable by induction.
liveness_properties: Termination: eventually all processes reach the terminated state.
model_bounds: N (the number of processes) is a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N is set to a specific finite value.
additional_assumptions: The specification includes a complete formal machine-checked proof that the correctness property is an invariant. The proof uses an inductive invariant that combines type correctness with two conditions: (1) any process that has completed its write step has value 1 in its register, and (2) either some process has not yet terminated, or some process read the value 1. The shared registers are assumed to be atomic (each read or write is an instantaneous action). The specification is also discussed in Section 7.2 of Lamport's 'Proving Safety Properties' document.
